title: Retire bronze_azureSQLdb2table — replace the last RefreshDataflow with a Copy activity so the pipeline is SPN-safe
description: Replace the pipeline's single remaining RefreshDataflow activity (bronze_procurement -> bronze_azureSQLdb2table) with two Copy activities reading dbo.procurement_transactional and dbo.supplier_ref from Azure SQL directly into bronze_procurement_transactional and bronze_supplier_ref. Retire the dataflow per .claude/rules/feature-retirement.md. This removes the last item in the pipeline that a service principal cannot refresh and that loses its credentials on every fabric-cicd publish.
acceptanceCriteria: The pipeline's `bronze_procurement` RefreshDataflow activity is gone, replaced by Copy activity/activities producing the SAME two bronze tables with the SAME names: `bronze_procurement_transactional` and `bronze_supplier_ref`.

The Copy source uses a Fabric Azure SQL connection (credential stored in Fabric's connection store, never in a tracked file) shared with the `Fabric-SPN-Access` security group — mirroring the two HttpServer connections that already run green under the SPN.

Incremental behaviour is preserved: the `p_from_date` pipeline parameter still drives a 7-day look-back window via a source query, and `p_from_date = '1900-01-01'` still means full load. If this moves to a different mechanism, the change is documented and the parameter contract stays intact.

The dataflow's `CorrectedDate` transformation — `#date(Day([Date])+2000, Month([Date]), Year([Date])-2000)`, a day/year swap correcting the source data — is relocated to bronze-to-silver, NOT dropped. A test or explicit verification shows the silver `Date` values are unchanged versus the pre-migration table.
Bronze row counts for both tables match the pre-migration values (capture the baseline BEFORE the first post-change pipeline run — it is one-shot and self-destructing, as task-038_2 learned).

`bronze_azureSQLdb2table` is retired per `.claude/rules/feature-retirement.md`: snapshot + manifest.json under `.claude/support/retired/`, commit pin, spec annotation, discoverability entry. Do NOT simply delete it.
A full pipeline run completes green end to end, with no RefreshDataflow activity remaining and therefore no SPN-refresh restriction and no credential-unbinding exposure on future publishes.

MECHANISM CHOSEN BY ERIK 2026-07-31 (inline, after being shown the fork): Copy activity, NOT a notebook. Rationale: task-035's notebook migration worked for EPI/WGI because those sources are PUBLIC HTTP with no credential to store. Azure SQL needs a secret at runtime, and there is no JDBC or secret-retrieval pattern anywhere in the repo (probed with a positive control). Key Vault is unusable here — the Azure subscription lives in tenant a7d750d0 (live.com#erikemilsson@hotmail.com) while Fabric is a different tenant, the same split that 401s the Fabric token and breaks 'Browse Azure'. A pipeline parameter or in-notebook password would put a credential in a tracked file, violating a hard invariant. A Copy activity stores the credential in Fabric's own connection store — the exact pattern already proven green under the SPN by bronzecopy_EUSupplyShares and bronzecopy_GlobalSupplyShares.

THE DATE FIX IS THE SUBTLE PART. The mashup builds CorrectedDate as #date(Day+2000, Month, Year-2000) — a deliberate day/year swap correcting malformed source dates — then DROPS the original `Date` and renames CorrectedDate to `Date`. A Copy activity cannot transform, so this must move. Preferred home is bronze-to-silver (keeps bronze raw, which is better medallion practice than pushing it into the source query). Whichever is chosen, criterion 4 requires proving silver dates are unchanged.

DESIGN FINDING (task-048, worth keeping): the relocated correction must run BEFORE the silver look-back window, not after. Everything downstream is expressed in CORRECTED-date space — bronze_load_metadata.last_load_date comes from silver_df.agg(F.max('date')), and window_min_date is the delete-insert boundary. Windowing raw dates against a corrected-space watermark would DELETE a range the append does not restore: silent data loss. The old SQL pushdown ("WHERE Date >= '{lookback_str}'") was therefore replaced with a DataFrame filter applied after correct_procurement_date. tests/test_procurement_dates.py::TestNotebookParity::test_notebook_corrects_before_windowing pins the ordering in the notebook TEXT, and TestIncrementalWindowEquivalence::test_windowing_on_raw_dates_is_wrong asserts the hazard still differs, so a future reorder fails locally instead of silently in Fabric.

FOURTH ERROR CATEGORY, 2026-07-31 — 'DATABASE NOT CURRENTLY AVAILABLE' = SERVERLESS AUTO-PAUSE, NOT A CREDENTIAL PROBLEM. Creating the Fabric Azure SQL connection failed with Fabric's generic wrapper 'We could not access the data source. Please make sure you have permission ... and that your credentials are correct' (status 400) — but the Details block read 'Database procurement-supplier-db on server procurement-supplier.database.windows.net is not currently available. Please retry the connection later.' The wrapper is boilerplate and actively misleading; ALWAYS read the Details block. Proof it was auto-pause: `az sql db show -g RG1 -s procurement-supplier -n procurement-supplier-db` returns skuName GP_S_Gen5 (the S = serverless), autoPauseDelay 60 (minutes), status Online, pausedDate null, resumedDate 2026-07-31T11:20:00Z. The error timestamp was 13:19:19 +0200 = 11:19:19Z — i.e. the attempt hit a paused DB, TRIGGERED the resume, and failed during the ~41s resume window. Retrying after the resume succeeds. Extends the existing taxonomy: 'Login failed for user X' = credential bound and wrong; 'Credentials are required to connect / Challenge type: Resource' = no credential bound; 'Login timeout expired / TCP Provider' = never reached the server (firewall/port); 'Database ... is not currently available' = reached the server, database paused or resuming, says NOTHING about the credential.

PIPELINE IMPLICATION OF autoPauseDelay=60 (assessed 2026-07-31, no change made): any pipeline run starting after >60 min of database inactivity will hit the resume window on its FIRST Copy attempt against Azure SQL. This is recurring, not one-off. Existing retry config already covers it — bronze_procurement carries retry=3 / retryIntervalInSeconds=300 (task-011), and a 5-minute retry interval comfortably exceeds the ~41s observed resume, so attempt 2 succeeds. The replacing Copy activities MUST inherit that retry policy; do not author them with retry=0. Disabling auto-pause (`az sql db update --auto-pause-delay -1`) would also fix it but bills continuously for a portfolio project, so it was deliberately NOT done. Note the first activity of a cold run may therefore always show one failed attempt in the run history — that is expected, not a regression.
